source: 1968 Chevrolet Chassis Service Manual, Steering, p.9-2

procedures.title: Manual steering gear lubricant: check and fill
steps: Pump in lubricant until it shows at the outboard screw hole; the gear is then at the correct level.
notes: Grease the steering linkage with water-resistant EP chassis lubricant every 6,000 miles or 6 months, whichever is first (lube points in Section 0).

procedures.title: Steering gear: adjust
steps: Before adjusting the gear for shimmy, loose or hard steering, check front alignment, shocks, wheel balance and tire pressure first.
Do the adjustments in the order below.
Remove the pitman arm nut, mark the arm's position relative to the sector shaft, and pull the arm with tool J-6632 (see figure 3 in the manual).
Loosen the lash adjuster screw locknut and back the adjuster screw out (counterclockwise) a few turns to unload the worm bearings (see figure 4 in the manual).
Turn the steering wheel gently one way to the stop, then back off about one turn.
Regular steering: take off the horn button or shroud and check preload with a torque wrench and 3/4 in. socket on the steering wheel nut (see figure 5 in the manual).
Tilt columns: disconnect the steering coupling, read the column's own torque, and subtract it from any reading taken through the gear.
Simulated wood wheels: remove the contact ring to reach the wheel nut.

Telescopic columns (Corvette): remove the horn button and check preload with a torque wrench and Phillips adapter socket on the star-headed screw at the wheel center, pressing lightly down on the wrench to keep the bit seated.
notes: Caution: never turn the wheel hard against the stops while the relay rod is disconnected; the ball guides can be damaged.
Use a torque wrench reading no higher than 100 lb-in maximum.
